\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بسته} \fa{بندی} \fa{کردن} (bastebandi kardan)}{بسته بندی کردن (bastebandi kardan)}]{\fa{بسته} \fa{بندی} \fa{کردن} (bastebandi kardan) — to pack, to package}

\label{lesson:FA-C262-bastebandi-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to lie down, then the Persian for to move house.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بسته} \fa{بندی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{بسته} \fa{بندی} \fa{کردن}} — \emph{bastebandi kardan} — \textquotedblleft{}to pack, to package\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bastebandi kardan} pairs \emph{bastebandi}, \textquotedblleft{}packing\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{kardan}. \emph{baste}, \textquotedblleft{}bundle\textquotedblright{} (from \emph{bastan}, \textquotedblleft{}to bind\textquotedblright{}), and \emph{bandi}, \textquotedblleft{}binding\textquotedblright{}, are both native. \emph{kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb, from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{صف} \fa{کشیدن} (saf keshidan)}{صف کشیدن (saf keshidan)}]{\fa{صف} \fa{کشیدن} (saf keshidan) — to queue}

\label{lesson:FA-C262-saf-keshidan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to move house, then the Persian for to pack.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{صف} \fa{کشیدن}}
\textbf{\fa{صف} \fa{کشیدن}} — \emph{saf keshidan} — \textquotedblleft{}to queue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{saf keshidan} is \textquotedblleft{}to draw a line\textquotedblright{}: \emph{saf} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṣaff}, \textquotedblleft{}row, rank\textquotedblright{} (root \emph{ṣ-f-f}, Lane), and \emph{keshidan}, \textquotedblleft{}to draw\textquotedblright{}, is native. \emph{keshidan}, \textquotedblleft{}to pull\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{kašīdan}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جریمه} \fa{شدن} (jarime shodan)}{جریمه شدن (jarime shodan)}]{\fa{جریمه} \fa{شدن} (jarime shodan) — to be fined}

\label{lesson:FA-C262-jarime-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to pack, then the Persian for to queue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جریمه} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{جریمه} \fa{شدن}} — \emph{jarime shodan} — \textquotedblleft{}to be fined\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{jarime shodan} pairs \emph{jarime}, borrowed from Arabic \emph{jarīma}, \textquotedblleft{}crime, offence\textquotedblright{} (root \emph{j-r-m}, Lane), with the Persian verb \emph{shodan}, \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}. \emph{shodan}, \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{šudan}, \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}. Persian uses it for the fine paid for an offence.
\end{cousinweb}
